rv.q: The staging has a subtlety verging on opacity.
The result is one of the season's most quietly devastating new American plays.
But one leaves “The Vessel” with the impression that the playwright felt required to put together a 90-minute play, but didn’t know how to fill it.
In spite of these excellent performers and all the effort expended, I sadly felt that The Vessel just did not contain very much.
The play offers its own thoughtful, if imperfect, meditation on the people who watch over it.
Brendan George’s well-intentioned play The Vessel, which has a lot to say but doesn’t say most of it in a theatrically exciting manner.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this drama about workers at the infamous Hudson Yards landmark. While some praise its thought-provoking exploration of tragedy and friendship, others find it overlong and unfocused despite earnest performances.
